frameworks.name: Two-Bucket Venture Investment Framework
frameworks.definition: ACQ Ventures categorizes early-stage investment targets into two buckets: existing-round companies already familiar with the founder's methodology seeking capital partnership, and bootstrapped operators seeking funding without requiring active management involvement.

frameworks.name: Founder Dependency Test
frameworks.definition: A diagnostic framework distinguishing revenue businesses (work without founder) from founder-dependent income sources; wealth creation requires the former.

claims.text: Alex Hormozi started ACQ Ventures (tech-focused venture arm) because existing deal flow exceeded what the prior capital structure could absorb; high-potential tech companies offered exits 5-10x larger than service businesses, allowing smaller equity positions to justify returns.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: High-potential tech companies with 5-10x+ exit potential
Smaller equity position acceptable due to exit size
claims.mechanism: Tech exits (5-10x+) allow capital-only investment without proportional equity dilution, reducing per-deal workload vs. service-business model that requires larger stakes for return justification
bounded_by: Does not apply to service businesses requiring large equity positions
Does not apply to bootstrapped operators avoiding founder exit

claims.text: ACQ Ventures' first investment bucket targets companies that have already raised a round and are familiar with the founder's existing methodology; these founders prefer the founder's capital over institutional VCs because they already consume his products and subscribe to his ideology.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Company has already raised prior round(s)
Founder familiarity with Alex Hormozi's existing products/ideology

claims.text: ACQ Ventures' second investment bucket targets bootstrapped founders who have proven product-market fit and seek capital to fund clear opportunities; these require minimal operational involvement and can be structured as capital-only investments.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Alex Hormozi structured ACQ Ventures as a self-funded personal vehicle rather than raising a traditional fund because check sizes and deal frequency were modest enough to deploy from existing capital without institutional LP overhead.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Deployment frequency low enough for personal capital to manage
bounded_by: Does not apply to large-scale fund structures requiring LP capital raise

claims.text: A founder's personal involvement in business operation is a liability, not an asset, for wealth creation; if the company dies when the founder is on vacation, the founder owns a leveraged job rather than an investable business.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Growth business where founder is primary revenue driver
No systemized operations independent of founder

claims.text: Businesses that require founder involvement to operate cannot scale beyond founder capacity; only businesses that work independently of the founder generate significant wealth and can be sold for outsized multiples.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: A business independent of the founder has value to external buyers; a founder-dependent business has value only to the founder (higher leverage income, not wealth creation)

claims.text: When evaluating investments, Alex Hormozi prioritizes acquiring companies and products that already demonstrate market traction and recurring revenue; adding capital to proven models ('putting gasoline on' existing success) outperforms building business systems that depend entirely on founder vision.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Target: existing revenue-generating businesses with proven product
claims.mechanism: Proven, compounding revenue with zero advertising overhead demonstrates independent market fit; capital deployed into such models scales faster and with less founder burden than models requiring founder to drive adoption
bounded_by: Does not apply to greenfield startups with novel markets
Does not apply to founder-dependent service businesses

claims.text: ACQ Ventures deployed approximately 6-8 deals totaling substantial capital within the first two months of operation, demonstrating rapid deal velocity driven by existing network and portfolio company deal flow.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.speaker_term: I've deployed a lot of money
conditions: Heavy reliance on existing network referrals

claims.text: A business model is only an asset (not personal income) when it generates revenue retention independent of founder presence; revenue retention is the diagnostic test for whether wealth creation is possible.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Owner evaluating long-term wealth vs short-term leverage
claims.mechanism: Revenue retention independent of founder = business has value to external acquirers; founder-dependent revenue = asset is valuable only to founder (no external liquidity)

examples.text: One portfolio company (School) demonstrated compounding revenue growth month-over-month with zero advertising spend. When capital was added to scale acquisition, revenue compounded even faster. This is the prototype for ACQ Ventures thesis: acquire proven, founder-independent business models and deploy capital to accelerate growth.

The alternative failure case: a business that only works because of the founder's personal effort. If the founder takes time off, revenue stops. This generates personal leverage and higher income but no transferable business value. Selling such a business yields minimal multiple because buyers purchase only the founder's time, not a systems-based operation.

practices.text: When evaluating a business investment, ask: 'Does this business require the founder to operate?' If yes, it is not an investable asset; if no, it is a business.
Structure venture investments to allow capital-only positions when the underlying business requires minimal management involvement and has clear deployment opportunity.
Solve for revenue retention first—ensuring the business operates independent of founder presence—before optimizing for growth or acquisition velocity.
